title: introduce-rag-bootcamp-starter-kit-with-serverless-executor-and-step-checks
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: onboarding engineers to RAG-driven features is still costly in time and noisy across infra boundaries. This PR adds a compact "bootcamp" starter kit that demonstrates end-to-end retrieval-augmented generation in a microservice pattern, with a serverless executor adapter, deterministic step assertions, and a small telemetry probe so learners can iterate quickly. The goal is a single dev flow that: 1) runs locally with a devcontainer, 2) exercises a minimal serverless runner (local lambda / function emulator), 3) includes stepwise checks that validate retrieval, prompt formatting, and structured output contracts, and 4) ships a smoke E2E test for CI. Summary of changes: - new quickstart template: quickstarts/rag-bootcamp/ with scenario manifests, step-check definitions, and example prompts - serverless adapter: examples/adapters/serverless-local/ that shows how to wire a function invocation into Redwood SDK tool-calling (TypeScript) - devcontainer and minimal Dockerfile: for one-command onboarding - telemetry probe: quickstarts/rag-bootcamp/telemetry/probes.md and a tiny shim that emits structured JSON events to stdout for local observability - smoke test: ci/smoke/rag-bootcamp-smoke.spec.ts (Playwright-style step runner) - docs: docs/bootcamp-guide.md with quick start instructions and recommended learning checkpoints Checklist: - [x] Add starter templates and adapters - [x] Add step-check assertions and example test cases - [x] Add devcontainer and runbook - [x] Add CI smoke test - [x] Add lightweight telemetry probe - [x] Docs and README (single-file quickstart guide) How to run locally (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-bootcamp 2) open in devcontainer or run ./scripts/start-dev.sh (spins local function emulator + Redis mock) 3) run ./scripts/run-demo.sh to step through prompts and see step checks 4) run npm run smoke to run CI-style smoke. Design notes: - Step-checks are deliberately deterministic and keyed to synthetic test vectors so learners see pass/fail feedback quickly without relying on networked LLMs. The kit includes an adapter shim that can be swapped from the synthetic LLM stub to Redwood hosted API with a single env var. - Serverless adapter demonstrates cold-start handling and short-lived KV caching semantics; it's intentionally minimal to avoid cloud costs. - Telemetry probe is designed to teach where to add span/context hooks; it's not a production agent. Related: this PR complements the smaller "authoring playground" kits by focusing on a linear learning path and CI smoke coverage for teams adopting RAG microservices.
